title.zh: 卷一百一十六 載記第十六 姚弋仲 姚襄 姚萇
title.en: Volume 116 Records 16: Yao Yizhong; Yao Xiang; Yao Chang
title.raw: 卷一百一十六 載記第十六 姚弋仲 姚襄 姚萇 Volume 116 Records 16: Yao Yizhong; Yao Xiang; Yao Chang

sentences.zh: 姚弋仲 姚襄 姚萇

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong; Yao Xiang; Yao Chang
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Yao Yizhong, Yao Xiang, and Yao Chang

sentences.zh: 姚弋仲，南安赤亭羌人也。

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong was a Qiang man from Chiting in Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong was a Qiang from Chiting in Nan'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先有虞氏之苗裔。

translations.literal: His ancestors were descendants of the Youyu clan.
translations.idiomatic: His line traced back to the ancient Youyu people.

sentences.zh: 禹封舜少子於西戎，世為羌酋。

translations.literal: Yu enfeoffed Shun's younger son in the western Rong; generation after generation they were Qiang chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu the Great enfeoffed a younger son of Shun among the western tribes, the family became hereditary Qiang chieftains.

sentences.zh: 其後燒當雄於洮、罕之間，七世孫填虞，漢中元末寇擾西州，為楊虛侯馬武所敗，徙出塞。

translations.literal: Later Shao Dang was mighty between Tao and Han; seventh-generation descendant Tian Yu, at Han's Zhongyuan end raided and disturbed the western province, was defeated by Marquis of Yangxu Ma Wu, moved out beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Shao Dang branch dominated the Tao and Han riverlands. Seven generations later Tian Yu raided the northwest at the end of the Han Zhongyuan era, was crushed by Ma Wu, Marquis of Yangxu, and was driven beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 虞九世孫遷那率種人內附，漢朝嘉之，假冠軍將軍、西羌校尉、歸順王，處之于南安之赤亭。

translations.literal: Yu's ninth-generation descendant Qian Na led his people to submit inward; the Han court praised him, appointed acting General Who Crowns the Army, Colonel of the Western Qiang, King Who Returns to Obedience, and settled them at Chiting in Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Nine generations on, Qian Na led his clansmen to submit to the Han, which honored him with the titles General Who Crowns the Army, Colonel of the Western Qiang, and King of Allegiance, and resettled the tribe at Chiting in Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 那玄孫柯回為魏鎮西將軍、綏戎校尉、西羌都督。

translations.literal: Na's great-great-grandson Ke Hui was Wei General Who Garrisons the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Rong, and Western Qiang Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His descendant Ke Hui served Wei as General Who Garrisons the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Rong, and commander of the Western Qiang.

sentences.zh: 回生弋仲，少英毅，不營產業，唯以收恤為務，眾皆畏而親之。

translations.literal: Hui fathered Yizhong, who from youth was heroic and resolute, did not manage estates, only took gathering and relief as task; the host all feared yet were close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Hui's son Yao Yizhong was bold and resolute from boyhood. He spurned private gain and devoted himself to succoring the needy; men feared his sternness yet loved him.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，東徙榆眉，戎夏繈負隨之者數萬，自稱護西羌校尉、雍州刺史、扶風公。

translations.literal: At the Yongjia turmoil, he moved east to Yumei; Rong and Xia swaddled-burden following him numbered tens of thousands; he styled himself Colonel Who Protects the Western Qiang, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Duke of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck in the Yongjia era he led his people east to Yumei, and tens of thousands of tribesmen and Chinese followed in his train. He declared himself Colonel Who Protects the Western Qiang, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 劉曜之平陳安也，以弋仲為平西將軍，封平襄公，邑之於隴上。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao pacified Chen An, he appointed Yizhong General Who Pacifies the West, enfeoffed him as Duke of Pingxiang, and granted him a fief on the Long plateau.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yao destroyed Chen An he named Yao Yizhong General Who Pacifies the West, invested him as Duke of Pingxiang, and settled his fief on the Long plateau.

sentences.zh: 及石季龍克上邽，弋仲說之曰：「明公握兵十萬，功高一時，正是行權立策之日。

translations.literal: When Shi Jilong took Shanggui, Yizhong persuaded him, saying: "Illustrious lord holds a hundred thousand troops, merit tops the age—this is exactly the day to wield power and set policy.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Hu captured Shanggui, Yao Yizhong urged him, "You command a hundred thousand veterans and stand above every rival—now is the moment to seize the initiative and lay long-term plans.

sentences.zh: 隴上多豪，秦風猛勁，道隆後服，道洿先叛，宜徙隴上豪強，虛其心腹，以實畿甸。

translations.literal: Longshang has many magnates; Qin wind is fierce and strong—where the way rises they submit late, where the way sinks they rebel first; ought to move Longshang's powerful clans, empty their heart-belly, to fill the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: The Long plateau teems with strongmen; Qin folk are fierce. They bow late when power waxes and rebel first when it wanes. Relocate those magnates from the heartland and settle them around the capital to strengthen the core.

sentences.zh: 」季龍納之，啟勒以弋仲行安西將軍、六夷左都督。

translations.literal: " Jilong accepted it, reported to Le to appoint Yizhong acting General Who Pacifies the West, Left Commander-in-Chief of the Six Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu agreed and petitioned Shi Le to name Yao Yizhong acting General Who Pacifies the West and left commander over the six barbarian corps.

sentences.zh: 後晉豫州刺史祖約奔於勒，勒禮待之，弋仲上疏曰：「祖約殘賊晉朝，逼殺太后，不忠於主，而陛下寵之，臣恐奸亂之萌，此其始矣。

translations.literal: Later Jin Inspector of Yuzhou Zu Yue fled to Le; Le treated him with courtesy; Yizhong submitted a memorial: "Zu Yue cruelly injured the Jin court, pressed to kill the empress dowager, was not loyal to his lord—yet Your Majesty favors him; your subject fears treacherous chaos's sprout—this is its beginning.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Yue of Jin defected, Shi Le honored him. Yao Yizhong memorialized: "Zu Yue ravaged the Jin court and hounded the empress dowager to her death. Rewarding such infidelity plants the seed of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」勒善之，後竟誅約。

translations.literal: " Le approved it; afterward in the end executed Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le accepted the advice and later executed Zu Yue.

sentences.zh: 勒既死，季龍執權，思弋仲之言，遂徙秦、雍豪傑于關東。

translations.literal: After Le died, Jilong grasped power, remembered Yizhong's words, thereupon moved Qin and Yong's heroes east of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Le's death Shi Hu took power, recalled Yao Yizhong's counsel, and resettled the great clans of Qin and Yong beyond the eastern passes.

sentences.zh: 弋仲率部眾數萬遷於清河，拜奮武將軍、西羌大都督，封襄平縣公。

translations.literal: Yizhong led a host of several tens of thousands moving to Qinghe, was appointed General Who Rouses Might, Grand Commander-in-Chief of the Western Qiang, enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangping county.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong brought tens of thousands of followers to Qinghe, received the titles General Who Rouses Might and commander of the Western Qiang, and was ennobled as Duke of Xiangping county.

sentences.zh: 及季龍廢石弘自立，弋仲稱疾不賀。

translations.literal: When Jilong deposed Shi Hong and established himself, Yizhong claimed illness and did not congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hu deposed Shi Hong and seized the throne, Yao Yizhong feigned illness and offered no congratulations.

sentences.zh: 季龍累召之，乃赴，正色謂季龍曰：「奈何把臂受託而反奪之乎！

translations.literal: Jilong repeatedly summoned him; then he came, with straight countenance said to Jilong: "How can you arm-in-arm receive entrustment yet in turn seize it!
translations.idiomatic: After repeated summons he appeared and rebuked Shi Hu: "How can you clasp a friend's arm in trust and then steal his throne?

sentences.zh: 」季龍憚其強正而不之責。

translations.literal: " Jilong feared his forceful rectitude and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu, respecting his blunt integrity, let the words pass.

sentences.zh: 遷持節、十郡六夷大都督、冠軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Promoted Bearer of the Staff, Grand Commander-in-Chief of Ten Commanderies and Six Yi, Grand General Who Crowns the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Bearer of the Staff, commander over ten commanderies and six barbarian corps, and Grand General Who Crowns the Army.

sentences.zh: 性清儉鯁直，不修威儀，屢獻讜言，無所回避，季龍甚重之。

translations.literal: By nature clear, frugal, and bluntly straight, he did not cultivate awe-inspiring deportment, repeatedly presented forthright words, nothing avoided; Jilong greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Austere, blunt, and indifferent to pomp, he spoke his mind without flinching, and Shi Hu held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 朝之大議，靡不參決，公卿亦憚而推下之。

translations.literal: Court's great deliberations, none in which he did not join decisions; dukes and ministers also feared and yielded below him.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in on every weighty policy debate, and even the great ministers deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 武城左尉，季龍寵姬之弟也，曾擾其部，弋仲執尉，數以迫脅之狀，命左右斬之。

translations.literal: Wucheng's Left Commandant was Jilong's favorite concubine's younger brother; he once harassed his troops; Yizhong seized the commandant, enumerated the coercion and threat circumstances, ordered attendants to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: The left commandant of Wucheng was the brother of Shi Hu's favorite concubine. When he molested Yao Yizhong's men, Yizhong seized him, listed his crimes, and ordered his immediate execution.

sentences.zh: 尉叩頭流血，左右諫，乃止。

translations.literal: The commandant knocked head bleeding; attendants remonstrated; then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The man begged until his brow bled; aides interceded, and Yizhong stayed the blade.

sentences.zh: 其剛直不回，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His firm straightness not turning—all was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Such unbending integrity was typical of him.

sentences.zh: 季龍末，梁犢敗李農于滎陽，季龍大懼，馳召弋仲。

translations.literal: Near Jilong's end, Liang Du defeated Li Nong at Xingyang; Jilong greatly feared, urgently summoned Yizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Shi Hu's reign Liang Du routed Li Nong at Xingyang. Terrified, Shi Hu urgently summoned Yao Yizhong.

sentences.zh: 弋仲率其部眾八千餘人屯於南郊，輕騎至鄴。

translations.literal: Yizhong led his host of more than eight thousand encamping at the southern suburb, light cavalry reaching Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong brought eight thousand warriors to camp south of the capital and rode ahead to Ye.

sentences.zh: 時季龍病，不時見弋仲，引入領軍省，賜其所食之食。

translations.literal: At the time Jilong was ill, did not promptly see Yizhong, led him into the commandant's bureau, granted him food from what he ate.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu was too ill for an audience and had him wait in the guard headquarters with a meal from the imperial table.

sentences.zh: 弋仲怒不食，曰：「召我擊賊，豈來覓食邪！

translations.literal: Yizhong angry did not eat, said: "You summon me to strike bandits—how could I come seeking food!
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong refused the food: "You called me to fight rebels, not to dine.

sentences.zh: 我不知上存亡，若一見，雖死無恨。

translations.literal: I do not know the sovereign's survival or death; if I see him once, though I die there is no regret.
translations.idiomatic: I do not know whether our lord still lives. Let me see him once and I can die content.

sentences.zh: 」左右言之，乃引見。

translations.literal: " Attendants spoke of it; then he was led to audience.
translations.idiomatic: When his escort relayed this, Shi Hu received him.

sentences.zh: 弋仲數季龍曰：「兒死來愁邪？

translations.literal: Yizhong rebuked Jilong: "Since the sons died, have you been grieving?
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong scolded Shi Hu: "Have you sickened yourself mourning your sons?

sentences.zh: 乃至於疾！

translations.literal: So much as to illness!
translations.idiomatic: Enough to fall ill?

sentences.zh: 兒小時不能使好人輔相，至令相殺。

translations.literal: When the sons were small you could not employ good men as assistants, until it reached mutual killing.
translations.idiomatic: You never gave your boys worthy tutors, and now they have murdered one another.

sentences.zh: 兒自有過，責其下人太甚，故反耳。

translations.literal: The sons themselves had faults; you blamed their subordinates too severely—therefore they rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Your sons were at fault, yet you punished their followers too harshly—that is why they turned on you.

sentences.zh: 汝病久，所立兒小，若不差，天下必亂。

translations.literal: You are long ill; the established son is small; if you do not recover, all under Heaven must be chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: You have been ill a long time and the heir is a child. If you do not recover, the realm will tear apart.

sentences.zh: 當宜憂此，不煩憂賊也。

translations.literal: Ought to worry about this; no need to trouble over bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Worry about that, not about Liang Du.

sentences.zh: 犢等因思歸之心，共為奸盜，所行殘賊，此成擒耳。

translations.literal: Du and others riding homesick hearts together act as treacherous bandits; what they do is cruel injury—this is ripe for capture.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Du's men are mutineers driven by homesickness; their cruelty makes them easy prey.

sentences.zh: 老羌請效死前鋒，使一舉而了。

translations.literal: This old Qiang begs to devote death at the vanguard, causing one stroke and finished.
translations.idiomatic: Let this old Qiang die in your vanguard and finish them in one blow.

sentences.zh: 」弋仲性狷直，俗無尊卑皆汝之，季龍恕而不責，於坐授使持節、侍中、征西大將軍，賜以鎧馬。

translations.literal: " Yizhong's nature was bluntly straight; custom without noble or base all called 'you'; Jilong forgave and did not blame; at the seat awarded Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Campaigns West, granted armor and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt to a fault, he addressed everyone as "you," high or low. Shi Hu only smiled and at table invested him as Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, and Grand General Who Campaigns West, with armor and a charger.

sentences.zh: 弋仲曰：「汝看老羌堪破賊以不？

translations.literal: Yizhong said: "You see whether old Qiang can break bandits or not?
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong asked, "Tell me, can this old Qiang still break your rebels?

sentences.zh: 」於是貫鉀跨馬於庭中，策馬南馳，不辭而出，遂滅梁犢。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he threaded armor and straddled horse in the courtyard, whipped horse galloping south, without farewell went out; thereupon destroyed Liang Du.
translations.idiomatic: He donned mail, leaped into the saddle in the courtyard, and galloped south without a word of leave, and annihilated Liang Du.

sentences.zh: 以功加劍履上殿，入朝不趨，進封西平郡公。

translations.literal: By merit added sword and shoes on hall, entering court not hastening, advanced enfeoffment Duke of Xiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For this feat he received the right to wear sword and shoes in court, enter without hurrying, and was promoted to Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 冉閔之亂，弋仲率眾討閔，次於混橋。

translations.literal: At Ran Min's turmoil, Yizhong led the host to punish Min, halted at Hun Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: During Ran Min's coup Yao Yizhong marched against him and camped at Hun Bridge.

sentences.zh: 石祗僭號于襄國，以弋仲為右丞相，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: Shi Zhi usurped title at Xiangguo, appointed Yizhong Right Chancellor, treated him with special rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi, who had declared himself emperor at Xiangguo, named Yao Yizhong Right Chancellor and honored him with exceptional ceremony.

sentences.zh: 祗與閔相攻，弋仲遣其子襄救祗，戒襄曰：「汝才十倍于閔，若不梟擒，不須復見我也。

translations.literal: Zhi and Min attacked each other; Yizhong sent his son Xiang to relieve Zhi, admonished Xiang: "Your talent is tenfold Ran Min's; if you do not owl-capture him, need not see me again.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Zhi and Ran Min clashed, Yao Yizhong sent Yao Xiang to the rescue with a warning: "You outmatch Ran Min tenfold. Bring me his head or do not return.

sentences.zh: 」襄擊閔于常盧澤，大破之而歸。

translations.literal: " Xiang attacked Min at Changlu Marsh, greatly defeated him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang met Ran Min at Changlu Marsh, routed him, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 弋仲怒襄之不擒閔也，杖之一百。

translations.literal: Yizhong was angry that Xiang had not captured Min, caned him one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Furious that Yao Xiang had not taken Ran Min prisoner, Yao Yizhong had him flogged one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 弋仲部曲馬何羅博學有文才，張豺之輔石世也，背弋仲歸豺，豺以為尚書郎。

translations.literal: Yizhong's follower Ma Heluo was broadly learned with literary talent; when Zhang Cai assisted Shi Shi, he turned his back on Yizhong and joined Cai; Cai appointed him Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Heluo, a client of Yao Yizhong, was a scholar. When Zhang Cai dominated the boy emperor Shi Shi, Ma deserted Yizhong for Zhang, who named him a secretary at the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 豺敗，復歸，咸勸殺之。

translations.literal: Cai defeated, he returned again; all urged killing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cai fell Ma came back; everyone urged his execution.

sentences.zh: 弋仲曰：「今正是招才納奇之日，當收其力用，不足害也。

translations.literal: Yizhong said: "Now is exactly the day to recruit talent and admit marvels; ought to gather his strength for use—not enough to harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong replied, "These are times to gather talent. Use his abilities; he is no threat.

sentences.zh: 」以為參軍。

translations.literal: " Appointed him army aide.
translations.idiomatic: He made him a staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 其寬恕如此。

translations.literal: His forgiveness was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 弋仲有子四十二人，常戒諸子曰：「吾本以晉室大亂，石氏待吾厚，故欲討其賊臣以報其德。

translations.literal: Yizhong had forty-two sons, often warned the sons: "I originally because the Jin house was greatly chaotic, the Shi clan treated me generously, therefore wished to punish their treacherous ministers to repay their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong fathered forty-two sons and often told them, "I served the Shi because they honored me while Jin collapsed, and I meant to purge their traitors in return.

sentences.zh: 今石氏已滅，中原無主，自古以來未有戎狄作天子者。

translations.literal: Now the Shi clan is already destroyed; the Central Plain has no lord; from antiquity until now there has never been Rong-Di making Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi are gone and the heartland has no ruler, yet no barbarian has ever ruled all China as Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 我死，汝便歸晉，當竭盡臣節，無為不義之事。

translations.literal: When I die, you then return to Jin; ought to exhaust ministerial integrity; do not do unrighteous matters.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, submit to Jin and serve with full loyalty. Do nothing dishonorable.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使請降。

translations.literal: " Thereupon sent envoys requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys to offer submission to Jin.

sentences.zh: 永和七年，拜弋仲使持節、六夷大都督、都督江、淮諸軍事、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、大單于，封高陵郡公。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yonghe, appointed Yizhong Bearer of the Staff, Grand Commander-in-Chief of Six Yi, Supervisor of Jiang and Huai Military Affairs, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, ceremony equal to Three Dukes, Great Chanyu, enfeoffed Duke of Gaoling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh Yonghe year Jin confirmed him as Bearer of the Staff, commander of the six barbarian hosts, director of Jiang and Huai operations, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with honors matching the Three Excellencies, Great Chanyu, and Duke of Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，時年七十三。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, died; at the time age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next year at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子襄之入關也，為苻生所敗，弋仲之柩為生所得，生以王禮葬之于天水冀縣。

translations.literal: When son Xiang entered the Pass, was defeated by Fu Sheng; Yizhong's coffin was obtained by Sheng; Sheng with kingly rites buried him in Tianshui Jixian.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xiang invaded Guanzhong Fu Sheng defeated him and seized Yao Yizhong's coffin, burying it with princely honors at Ji in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 萇僭位，追諡曰景元皇帝，廟號始祖，墓曰高陵，置園邑五百家。

translations.literal: Chang usurped throne, posthumously titled Emperor Jingyuan, temple name First Ancestor, tomb called Gaoling, established park settlement five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Chang took the throne he posthumously named his father Emperor Jingyuan, temple name Progenitor, with a mausoleum called Gaoling and a guard colony of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 襄字景國，弋仲之第五子也。

translations.literal: Xiang, styled Jingguo, was Yizhong's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang, courtesy name Jingguo, was the fifth son of Yao Yizhong.

sentences.zh: 年十七，身長八尺五寸，臂垂過膝，雄武多才藝，明察善撫納，士眾愛敬之，咸請為嗣。

translations.literal: At age seventeen, body eight chi five cun tall, arms hung past knees, heroic and martial with many talents, clear-sighted and good at comforting and receiving; officers and host loved and revered him, all asked him to be heir.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he stood eight and a half chi, his arms reached past his knees, and he combined martial prowess with many skills. Keen-eyed and winning in manner, soldiers loved him and urged that he succeed his father.

sentences.zh: 弋仲弗許，百姓固請者日有千數，乃授之以兵。

translations.literal: Yizhong did not permit; common people firmly requesting daily numbered in thousands; thereupon entrusted him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong refused until thousands petitioned daily; then he gave Yao Xiang a command.

sentences.zh: 石祗僭號，以襄為使持節、驃騎將軍、護烏丸校尉、豫州刺史、新昌公。

translations.literal: Shi Zhi usurped title, appointed Xiang Bearer of the Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, Colonel Who Protects the Wuhuan, Inspector of Yuzhou, Duke of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi named him Bearer of the Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, Wuhuan colonel, Inspector of Yuzhou, and Duke of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 晉遣使拜襄持節、平北將軍、并州刺史、即丘縣公。

translations.literal: Jin sent envoys appointing Xiang Staff Bearer, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Bingzhou, Duke of Jiuqiu county.
translations.idiomatic: Jin invested him with the staff, the title General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Bingzhou, and Duke of Jiuqiu county.

sentences.zh: 弋仲死，襄秘不發喪，率戶六萬南攻陽平、元城、發幹，皆破之，殺掠三千餘家，屯於碻磝津。

translations.literal: When Yizhong died, Xiang kept it secret and did not announce mourning, led sixty thousand households south attacking Yangping, Yuancheng, Fagan, all broke them, killed and plundered more than three thousand households, encamped at Qiao'ao Ford.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Yizhong died Yao Xiang concealed the death, took sixty thousand households south, stormed Yangping, Yuancheng, and Fagan, slaughtered more than three thousand families, and camped at the Qiao'ao crossing.

sentences.zh: 以太原王亮為長史，天水尹赤為司馬，略陽伏子成為左部帥，南安斂岐為右部帥，略陽黑那為前部帥，強白為後部帥，太原薛贊、略陽王權翼為參軍。

translations.literal: Appointed Taiyuan Wang Liang Chief Clerk, Tianshui Yin Chi Major, Lueyang Fuzicheng Left Division Commander, Nan'an Lianqi Right Division Commander, Lueyang Heina Forward Division Commander, Qiang Bai Rear Division Commander, Taiyuan Xue Zan and Lueyang Wang Quanyi as army aides.
translations.idiomatic: He named Wang Liang of Taiyuan chief clerk, Yin Chi of Tianshui army major, Fuzicheng of Lueyang commander of the left wing, Lianqi of Nan'an of the right, Heina of Lueyang of the vanguard, Qiang Bai of the rear, and Xue Zan and Quan Yi as staff advisers.

sentences.zh: 南至滎陽，始發喪行服。

translations.literal: South reaching Xingyang, then announced mourning and observed garments.
translations.idiomatic: Only at Xingyang did he announce his father's death and don mourning.

sentences.zh: 與高昌、李曆戰于麻田，馬中流矢死，賴其弟萇以免。

translations.literal: Fought Gao Chang and Li Li at Matian; horse was struck by stray arrow and died; relied on younger brother Chang to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Against Gao Chang and Li Li at Matian his mount was killed by an arrow; only his brother Yao Chang saved him.

sentences.zh: 晉處襄於譙城，遣五弟為任，單騎度淮，見豫州刺史謝尚于壽春。

translations.literal: Jin placed Xiang at Qiaocheng, sent fifth younger brother as hostage, single horse crossed the Huai, met Inspector of Yuzhou Xie Shang at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Jin quartered him at Qiao, took his fifth brother as hostage, and Yao Xiang rode alone across the Huai to meet Xie Shang, Inspector of Yuzhou, at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 尚命去仗衛，幅巾以待之，一面交款，便若平生。

translations.literal: Shang ordered removed arms and guards, headcloth to await him; one meeting exchanged sincerity, then like lifelong friends.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang dismissed arms and escort, received him in simple dress, and at first meeting they spoke as old friends.

sentences.zh: 襄少有高名，雄武冠世，好學博通，雅善談論，英濟之稱著于南夏。

translations.literal: Xiang from youth had high fame, heroic martial crown of the age, fond of learning broadly penetrating, elegantly skilled in discourse; hero-and-helper's title was manifest in southern Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned while young, unmatched in arms, learned and eloquent, Yao Xiang was hailed as a champion of the south.

sentences.zh: 中軍將軍、揚州刺史殷浩憚其威名，乃因襄諸弟，頻遣刺客殺襄，刺客皆推誠告實，襄待之若舊。

translations.literal: Central Army General, Inspector of Yangzhou Yin Hao feared his awesome name; thereupon through Xiang's various younger brothers, repeatedly sent assassins to kill Xiang; assassins all pushed sincerity telling truth; Xiang treated them as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao, general of the central army and governor of Yangzhou, envied his fame and repeatedly sent killers through Yao Xiang's brothers; each assassin confessed and Yao Xiang treated him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 浩潛遣將軍魏憬率五千餘人襲襄，襄乃斬憬而並其眾。

translations.literal: Hao secretly sent General Wei Jing leading more than five thousand to raid Xiang; Xiang thereupon beheaded Jing and annexed his host.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao secretly sent Wei Jing with five thousand men; Yao Xiang slew Wei Jing and absorbed his troops.

sentences.zh: 浩愈惡之，乃使將軍劉啟守譙，遷襄于梁國蠡台，表授梁國內史。

translations.literal: Hao increasingly hated him, therefore sent General Liu Qi to guard Qiao, moved Xiang to Liang state's Litai, memorialized appointing Liang Interior Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao then garrisoned Qiao under Liu Qi, moved Yao Xiang to Litai in Liang, and had him named interior clerk of Liang.

sentences.zh: 襄遣權翼詣浩，浩曰：「姚平北每舉動自由，豈所望也。

translations.literal: Xiang sent Wang Quanyi to visit Hao; Hao said: "General Who Pacifies the North Yao's every movement is free—how is this what is hoped.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang sent Quan Yi to Yin Hao, who complained, "Your General Who Pacifies the North does as he pleases—hardly what we expect.

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「將軍輕納奸言，自生疑貳，愚謂猜嫌之由，不在於彼。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "The general lightly accepts slanderous words, himself breeds suspicion and double-mindedness; foolishly I say the source of mistrust is not in him.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi replied, "You credit malicious gossip and breed your own suspicions. The fault is not his.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「姚君縱放小人，盜竊吾馬，王臣之體固若是乎？

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Lord Yao indulges petty men stealing my horses—is royal minister's deportment indeed thus?
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao said, "He lets his men steal my horses—is that fitting for a servant of the throne?

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「將軍謂姚平北以威武自強，終為難保，校兵練眾，將懲不恪，取馬者欲以自衛耳。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "The general thinks General Who Pacifies the North by might and awe strengthens self, in the end hard to guarantee; drills troops and trains host, about to punish lack of reverence; those who took horses wished to use for self-defense only.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi said, "You fear Yao Xiang will rely on force and prove untrustworthy. He drills his troops to punish slack discipline; the horses were taken for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「何至是也。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "How could it reach this.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao said, "Surely not.

sentences.zh: 」浩遣謝萬討襄，襄逆擊破之。

translations.literal: " Hao sent Xie Wan to punish Xiang; Xiang intercepted and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao sent Xie Wan against him; Yao Xiang met him and won.

sentences.zh: 浩甚怒，會聞關中有變，浩率眾北伐，襄乃要擊浩于山桑，大敗之，斬獲萬計，收其資仗。

translations.literal: Hao greatly angry; it happened they heard Guanzhong had turmoil; Hao led the host north to campaign; Xiang then intercepted and attacked Hao at Shansang, greatly defeated him, beheaded and captured counted in ten thousands, seized his supplies and arms.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao was furious. When unrest drew him north on campaign, Yao Xiang ambushed him at Shansang, shattered his army, took ten thousand heads, and captured his baggage and weapons.

sentences.zh: 使兄益守山桑壘，復如淮南。

translations.literal: Ordered elder brother Yi guard Shansang rampart, again went to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He left his brother Yao Yi to hold Shansang and returned toward Huainan.

sentences.zh: 浩遣劉啟、王彬之伐山桑，襄自淮南擊滅之，鼓行濟淮，屯於盱眙，招掠流人，眾至七萬，分置守宰，勸課農桑，遣使建鄴，罪狀殷浩，並自陳謝。

translations.literal: Hao sent Liu Qi and Wang Binzhi to attack Shansang; Xiang from Huainan struck and destroyed them, drum-marching crossed the Huai, encamped at Xuyi, summoned and plundered displaced people, host reached seventy thousand, divided and placed guards and magistrates, urged and supervised farming and sericulture, sent envoys to Jiankang, indicted Yin Hao, and also self-explained apology.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao sent Liu Qi and Wang Binzhi against Shansang; Yao Xiang marched from Huainan, destroyed them, crossed the Huai with drums beating, and camped at Xuyi. He rallied refugees until his host reached seventy thousand, appointed local officials, promoted farming, and sent envoys to the capital accusing Yin Hao while offering his own apology.

sentences.zh: 流人郭斁等千餘人執晉堂邑內史劉仕降於襄，朝延大震，以吏部尚書周閔為中軍將軍，緣江備守。

translations.literal: Displaced people Guo Yi and others more than a thousand seized Jin Tangyi Interior Clerk Liu Shi and surrendered to Xiang; court-extension greatly quaked; appointed Minister of Personnel Zhou Min as Central Army General, along the river prepared defense.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand refugees led by Guo Yi seized Liu Shi, interior clerk of Tangyi, and defected to Yao Xiang. The court was shaken and named Zhou Min of the Ministry of Personnel general of the central army to guard the Yangzi line.

sentences.zh: 襄將佐部眾皆北人，咸勸襄北還。

translations.literal: Xiang's generals, aides, and host were all northern men; all urged Xiang to return north.
translations.idiomatic: His officers and troops were northerners and urged him to march home.

sentences.zh: 襄方軌北引，自稱大將軍、大單于，進攻外黃，為晉邊將所敗。

translations.literal: Xiang parallel-tracks led north, styled himself Grand General, Great Chanyu, advanced to attack Waihuang, was defeated by Jin border generals.
translations.idiomatic: He turned north as Grand General and Great Chanyu, struck Waihuang, and was beaten by Jin frontier troops.

sentences.zh: 襄收散卒而勤撫恤之，於是復振。

translations.literal: Xiang gathered scattered soldiers and diligently comforted them; thereupon revived.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the fugitives, tended them kindly, and his strength returned.

sentences.zh: 乃據許昌，將如河東以圖關右，自許遂攻洛陽，逾月不克。

translations.literal: Thereupon held Xuchang, was about to go to Hedong to plot Guan-you; from Xu then attacked Luoyang; over a month did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Xuchang, meant to cross into Hedong and win the northwest, but from Xuchang attacked Luoyang and failed for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 其長史王亮諫襄曰：「公英略蓋天下，士眾思效力命，不可損威勞眾，守此孤城。

translations.literal: His Chief Clerk Wang Liang remonstrated Xiang: "Lord's heroic strategy covers all under Heaven; officers and host wish to devote strength and life—cannot harm awe and weary the host, guarding this lone city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang urged him, "Your genius spans the realm and your men yearn to serve. Do not waste prestige and troops on this isolated city.

sentences.zh: 宜還河北，以弘遠略。

translations.literal: Ought to return north of the River, to expand far-reaching strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw north of the Yellow River and pursue the larger design.

sentences.zh: 」襄曰：「洛陽雖小，山河四塞之固，亦是用武之地。

translations.literal: " Xiang said: "Though Luoyang is small, mountains and rivers four-blockade firm—it is also terrain for wielding arms.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang replied, "Luoyang is small but ringed by natural barriers—a true seat of war.

sentences.zh: 吾欲先據洛陽，然後開建大業。

translations.literal: I wish first to hold Luoyang, then open and establish great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to take Luoyang first, then build the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 」俄而亮卒，襄哭之甚慟，曰：「天將不欲成吾事乎？

translations.literal: " Shortly Liang died; Xiang wept for him very bitterly, said: "Is Heaven about to not wish to complete my affair?
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Liang died. Yao Xiang wailed, "Does Heaven forbid my success?

sentences.zh: 王亮舍我去也！」

translations.literal: Wang Liang has left me!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang has abandoned me!"

sentences.zh: 晉征西大將軍桓溫自江陵伐襄，戰于伊水北，為溫所敗，率麾下數千騎奔於北山。

translations.literal: Jin's Grand General Who Campaigns West Huan Wen from Jiangling campaigned against Xiang, fought north of the Yi River, was defeated by Huan Wen, led several thousand riders under his command fleeing to North Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen marched from Jiangling, met Yao Xiang north of the Yi River, broke him, and Yao Xiang fled into the northern hills with a few thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 其夜，百姓棄妻子隨襄者五千餘人，屯據陽鄉，赴者又四千餘戶。

translations.literal: That night, common people abandoning wives and children following Xiang were more than five thousand, encamped and held Yangxiang; those who came were another more than four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: That night over five thousand civilians left families to follow him at Yangxiang, and four thousand more households soon joined.

sentences.zh: 襄前後敗喪數矣，眾知襄所在，輒扶老攜幼賓士而赴之。

translations.literal: Xiang before and after defeat and loss several times; the host knowing where Xiang was, then helped old carrying young guest-gentleman-like hastening to him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yao Xiang had suffered many defeats, whenever people learned where he was they hurried old and young alike to his camp.

sentences.zh: 時或傳襄創重不濟，溫軍所得士女莫不北望揮涕。

translations.literal: At times rumor spread that Xiang's wounds were grave and he would not recover; among the men and women taken by Wen's army there was none who did not look north and wipe tears.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time word ran that Yao Xiang's wounds were mortal and he would not survive; every soldier's wife and captive commoner in Huan Wen's host gazed northward and wept.

sentences.zh: 其得物情如此。

translations.literal: Thus did he win the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the devotion he commanded among the people.

sentences.zh: 先是，弘農楊亮歸襄，襄待以客禮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Liang of Hongnong had come over to Xiang, and Xiang treated him with guest courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Liang of Hongnong had defected to Yao Xiang, who received him with the rites due an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 後奔桓溫，溫問襄於亮，亮曰：「神明器宇，孫策之儔，而雄武過之。

translations.literal: Later he fled to Huan Wen; Wen asked Liang about Xiang, and Liang said: "In divine bearing and imposing presence he is a match for Sun Ce, yet in heroic martial prowess he surpasses him.
translations.idiomatic: He later fled to Huan Wen, who asked Yang Liang what manner of man Yao Xiang was. Liang replied, "He has the aura of a born leader—Sun Ce's peer, and even more formidable in arms."

sentences.zh: 」其見重如是。

translations.literal: Thus was he esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem he inspired.

sentences.zh: 萇字景茂，弋仲第二十四子也。

translations.literal: Chang, courtesy name Jingmao, was Yizhong's twenty-fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang, whose courtesy name was Jingmao, was the twenty-fourth son of Yao Yizhong.

sentences.zh: 少聰哲，多權略，廓落任率，不修行業，諸兄皆奇之。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and wise, full of stratagems, broad-minded and unrestrained, and did not cultivate conduct; his elder brothers all marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was sharp and resourceful, fond of schemes yet openhanded and free in his ways, careless of formal self-cultivation; each of his older brothers regarded him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 隨襄征伐，每參大謀。

translations.literal: He followed Xiang on campaigns and always took part in great plans.
translations.idiomatic: He rode with Yao Xiang on every campaign and was consulted on the weightiest decisions.

sentences.zh: 襄之寇洛陽也，夢萇服袞衣，升御坐，諸酋長皆侍立，旦謂將佐曰：「吾夢如此，此兒志度不恆，或能大起吾族。

translations.literal: When Xiang raided Luoyang, he dreamed that Chang wore ceremonial robes, ascended the imperial seat, and all the chieftains stood attendance; at dawn he told his officers: "My dream was thus—this boy's aims and bearing are not ordinary; perhaps he can greatly raise our clan.
translations.idiomatic: While Yao Xiang was striking toward Luoyang he dreamed that Yao Chang stood robed as an emperor on the throne while tribal chiefs waited on him in ranks. At daybreak he told his staff, "I have seen such a dream. The lad's ambition is no common thing; he may yet exalt our whole line."

sentences.zh: 」襄之敗于麻田也，馬中流矢死，萇下馬以授襄，襄曰：「汝何以自免？

translations.literal: " When Xiang was defeated at Madian, his horse was struck by a flying arrow and died; Chang dismounted and gave his mount to Xiang. Xiang said: "How will you save yourself?
translations.idiomatic: After the rout at Madian, Yao Xiang's horse was killed by a stray shaft; Yao Chang sprang down and pressed the reins into his brother's hand. Yao Xiang cried, "And how will you get away?"

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「但令兄濟，豎子安敢害萇！

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Only let elder brother be delivered—how would some wretch dare harm Chang!
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang answered, "If you ride clear, no pack of nobodies will touch me."

sentences.zh: 」會救至，俱免。

translations.literal: " When rescue arrived, both escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Relief came in time, and both men survived.

sentences.zh: 及襄死，萇率諸弟降于苻生。

translations.literal: When Xiang died, Chang led his younger brothers to surrender to Fu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Xiang fell, Yao Chang brought their brothers to submit to Fu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 苻堅以萇為揚武將軍。

translations.literal: Fu Jian appointed Chang General Who Raises Might.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian named him General Who Raises Might.

sentences.zh: 曆左衛將軍，隴東、汲郡、河東、武都、武威、巴西、扶風太守，甯、幽、兗三州刺史，復為揚武將軍，步兵校尉，封益都侯。

translations.literal: He successively served as General of the Left Guard, Administrator of Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Wuwei, Baxi, and Fufeng, Inspector of three provinces—Ning, You, and Yan—was again General Who Raises Might and Colonel of Foot Soldiers, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through General of the Left Guard, magistracies across Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Wuwei, Baxi, and Fufeng, and inspectorships of Ning, You, and Yan, then returned to the rank of General Who Raises Might and Colonel of Foot Soldiers, with a marquisate at Yidu.

sentences.zh: 為堅將，累有大功。

translations.literal: As Jian's general, he repeatedly achieved great merit.
translations.idiomatic: As Fu Jian's commander he won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 初，萇隨楊安伐蜀，嘗晝寢水旁，上有神光煥然，左右咸異之。

translations.literal: At first, when Chang followed Yang An to campaign against Shu, he once napped by day beside the water; above him a divine light shone brilliantly, and those around him all thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, while serving under Yang An in the conquest of Shu, Yao Chang dozed by a stream at noon; a supernatural radiance played above him, and every man in his escort knew it for an omen.

sentences.zh: 及苻堅寇晉，以萇為龍驤將軍、督益、梁州諸軍事，謂萇曰：「朕本以龍驤建業，龍驤之號未曾假人，今特以相授，山南之事一以委卿。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian invaded Jin, he made Chang Dragon-Soaring General and supervisor of military affairs in Yi and Liang, and said to Chang: "I originally founded my enterprise with the title Dragon-Soaring; I have never lent that style to another—now I specially confer it on you; all matters south of the mountains I wholly entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian marched against Jin he invested Yao Chang as Dragon-Soaring General and gave him command of all forces in Yi and Liang. "The Dragon-Soaring banner built my throne," he said. "I have never given that name away; now it is yours alone. South of the Qinling ridges, your word is law."

sentences.zh: 」堅左將軍竇沖進曰：「王者無戲言，此將不祥之征也，惟陛下察之。

translations.literal: " Fu Jian's General of the Left Dou Chong advanced and said: "A king has no jesting words—this generalship is an ill omen; I beg Your Majesty to consider it.
translations.idiomatic: His general Dou Chong stepped forward. "Sovereigns do not speak in sport," he warned. "That commission is a dark portent. I urge you to reconsider."

sentences.zh: 」堅默然。

translations.literal: " Jian was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said nothing.

sentences.zh: 堅既敗於淮南，歸長安，慕容泓起兵叛堅。

translations.literal: After Jian was defeated at Huainan and returned to Chang'an, Murong Hong raised troops in rebellion against Jian.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's defeat in Huainan, he withdrew to Chang'an; Murong Hong then rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 堅遣子叡討之，以萇為司馬。

translations.literal: Jian sent his son Rui to punish him and made Chang marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent his son Fu Rui against the rebels and named Yao Chang his army marshal.

sentences.zh: 為泓所敗，叡死之。

translations.literal: He was defeated by Hong, and Rui died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hong shattered the expedition, and Fu Rui died on the field.

sentences.zh: 萇遣龍驤長史趙都詣堅謝罪，堅怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Chang sent Dragon-Soaring chief clerk Zhao Du to Jian to apologize for his fault; Jian in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang sent his chief clerk Zhao Du to apologize; Fu Jian, furious, had Zhao executed.

sentences.zh: 萇懼，奔於渭北，遂如馬牧。

translations.literal: Chang feared and fled to the north of the Wei, then went to the horse pastures.
translations.idiomatic: Terror-stricken, Yao Chang bolted across the Wei to the northern pastures.

sentences.zh: 西州豪族尹詳、趙曜、王欽盧、王欽盧、牛雙、狄廣、張乾等率五萬餘家，咸推萇為盟主。

translations.literal: Powerful western clans Yin Xiang, Zhao Yao, Wang Qinlu, Wang Qinlu, Niu Shuang, Di Guang, Zhang Qian, and others led more than fifty thousand households and all pushed Chang to be covenant lord.
translations.idiomatic: Western magnates—Yin Xiang, Zhao Yao, Wang Qinlu, Wang Qinlu (named twice in the text), Niu Shuang, Di Guang, Zhang Qian, and their following—mobilized over fifty thousand households and hailed Yao Chang as their league chief.

sentences.zh: 萇將距之，天水尹緯說萇曰：「今百六之數既臻，秦亡之兆已見，以將軍威靈命世，必能匡濟時艱，故豪傑驅馳，咸同推仰。

translations.literal: Chang was about to refuse them; Yin Wei of Tianshui persuaded Chang, saying: "Now the cycle of great calamity has arrived, and the omen of Qin's fall is already manifest; by the general's awe-inspiring mandate over the age you are sure to rescue the age from hardship—therefore heroes gallop to you and together lift you up.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang meant to decline, but Yin Wei of Tianshui urged him on: "The great reckoning is upon us and Former Qin is doomed. Your prestige commands the hour; every bold spirit rallies to you because they believe you alone can save the realm."

sentences.zh: 明公宜降心從議，以副群望，不可坐觀沈溺而不拯救之。

translations.literal: The enlightened lord ought to humble his mind and follow their counsel, to match the multitude's hopes; you cannot sit watching them sink and drown without rescuing them.
translations.idiomatic: Humble your pride, accept their mandate, and answer the hope of the world. You must not watch them founder and do nothing.

sentences.zh: 」萇乃從緯謀，乙太元九年自稱大將軍、大單于、萬年秦王，大赦境內，年號白雀，稱制行事。

translations.literal: " Chang then followed Wei's plan; in the ninth year of Jin's Taiyuan era he styled himself Grand General, Great Chanyu, and Prince of Wannian of Qin, proclaimed an amnesty within his borders, adopted the era name White Sparrow, and exercised imperial authority in conducting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang took Yin Wei's counsel. In the ninth year of the Eastern Jin Taiyuan era he declared himself Grand General, Great Chanyu, and Prince of Wannian of Qin, ordered a general amnesty, chose the reign title White Sparrow, and ruled as regent.

sentences.zh: 以天水尹詳、南安龐演為左右長史，南安姚晃、尹緯為左右司馬，天水狄伯支、焦虔、梁希、龐魏、任謙為從事中郎，姜訓、閻遵為掾屬，王據、焦世、蔣秀、尹延年、牛雙、張乾為參軍，王欽盧、姚方成、王破虜、楊難、尹嵩、裴騎、趙曜、狄廣、黨刪等為帥。

translations.literal: He appointed Yin Xiang of Tianshui and Pang Yan of Nan'an as left and right senior clerks; Yao Huang of Nan'an and Yin Wei as left and right majors; Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, and Ren Qian of Tianshui as attendant clerks; Jiang Xun and Yan Zun as staff aides; Wang Ju, Jiao Shi, Jiang Xiu, Yin Yannian, Niu Shuang, and Zhang Qian as military advisers; and Wang Qinlu, Yao Fangcheng, Wang Polu, Yang Nan, Yin Song, Pei Qi, Zhao Yao, Di Guang, Dang Shan, and others as commanders.
translations.idiomatic: He named Yin Xiang of Tianshui and Pang Yan of Nan'an his senior clerks, Yao Huang and Yin Wei his majors, Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, and Ren Qian attendant clerks, Jiang Xun and Yan Zun administrative aides, Wang Ju, Jiao Shi, Jiang Xiu, Yin Yannian, Niu Shuang, and Zhang Qian staff advisers, and Wang Qinlu, Yao Fangcheng, Wang Polu, Yang Nan, Yin Song, Pei Qi, Zhao Yao, Di Guang, Dang Shan, and the rest brigade commanders.

sentences.zh: 時慕容沖與苻堅相攻，眾甚盛。

translations.literal: At the time Murong Chong and Fu Jian attacked each other, and Chong's host was very large.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong and Fu Jian were locked in war, and Chong's army had swollen to vast numbers.

sentences.zh: 萇將西上，恐沖遏之，乃遣使通和，以子崇為質於沖，進屯北地，厲兵積粟，以觀時變。

translations.literal: Chang was about to march west and feared Chong would block him, so he sent envoys to open peace and gave his son Chong as hostage to Chong; he advanced and encamped at Beidi, sharpened weapons and stored grain, to watch how the times shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Planning a drive westward, Yao Chang feared Murong Chong might bar his path. He sued for truce, left his son Yao Chong as hostage, moved his camp to Beidi, drilled his troops and filled his granaries, and waited for the political weather to break.

sentences.zh: 苻堅先徙晉人李祥等數千戶于敷陸，至是，降於萇，北地、新平、安定羌胡降者十餘萬戶。

translations.literal: Fu Jian had earlier relocated several thousand households of Jin people such as Li Xiang to Fulu; at this time they surrendered to Chang, and Qiang and Hu who submitted in Beidi, Xinping, and An Ding numbered more than a hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian had once resettled several thousand Jin households led by Li Xiang at Fulu; they now came over to Yao Chang, and more than a hundred thousand Qiang and Hu households in Beidi, Xinping, and Anding followed suit.

sentences.zh: 堅率諸將攻之，不能克。

translations.literal: Jian led his generals to attack him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian threw his generals against him but could not break his lines.

sentences.zh: 萇聞容慕沖攻長安，議進趨之計，群下咸曰：「宜先據咸陽以制天下。

translations.literal: When Chang heard that Rong Muchong was attacking Chang'an, he deliberated plans for advancing thither; his subordinates all said: "We ought first to seize Xianyang to control the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Murong Chong was storming Chang'an, Yao Chang called council. His officers urged, "Seize Xianyang first and the empire is yours to steer."

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「燕因懷舊之士而起兵，若功成事捷，咸有東歸之思，安能久固秦川！

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Yan raised arms relying on men who long for the old; if they achieve merit and succeed, all will harbor thoughts of returning east—how could they long hold firm in the Qin riverlands!
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang objected. "Yan feeds on nostalgia. Once they win, every soldier will dream of home in the east. They cannot hold the Guanzhong basin for long."

sentences.zh: 吾欲移兵嶺北，廣收資實，須秦弊燕回，然後垂拱取之。

translations.literal: I wish to shift troops north of the ridges, broadly gather resources and supplies, wait until Qin is exhausted and Yan withdraws, then take it hands-folded.
translations.idiomatic: I will shift my host beyond the northern ranges, gather strength and stores, and let Former Qin bleed while Yan marches away—then I can take Guanzhong without striking a blow.

sentences.zh: 兵不血刃，坐定天下，此卞莊得二之義也。

translations.literal: Weapons not bloodied, sit and settle the realm—this is the meaning of Bian Zhuang gaining two.
translations.idiomatic: To settle the empire from a chair, blades unstained—that is Bian Zhuang's trick of letting two tigers tear each other.

sentences.zh: 」堅甯朔將軍宋方率騎三千從雲中將赴長安，萇自貳縣要破之，方單馬奔免，其司馬田晃率眾降萇。

translations.literal: " Fu Jian's General Who Calms the North Song Fang led three thousand horse from Yunzhong intending to hurry to Chang'an; Chang intercepted and destroyed him at Er County; Fang alone on horseback fled and escaped, and his major Tian Huang led the host to surrender to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's General Who Calms the North, Song Fang, was racing from Yunzhong toward Chang'an with three thousand riders when Yao Chang ambushed him at Er County. Song Fang escaped alone; his major Tian Huang surrendered the column.

sentences.zh: 萇遣諸將攻新平，克之，因略地至安定，嶺北諸城盡降之。

translations.literal: Chang sent generals to attack Xinping, took it, then raided territory to An Ding; all cities north of the ridges submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang's generals stormed Xinping, swept on to Anding, and every fortress north of the ranges opened its gates.

sentences.zh: 時苻堅為慕容沖所逼，走入五將山。

translations.literal: At the time Fu Jian was pressed by Murong Chong and fled into Mount Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian, harried by Murong Chong, fled into the Wujiang hills.

sentences.zh: 沖入長安。

translations.literal: Chong entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong took Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 堅司隸校尉權翼、尚書趙遷、大鴻臚皇甫覆、光祿大夫薛贊、扶風太守段鏗等文武數百人奔於萇。

translations.literal: Jian's Metropolitan Governor Quan Yi, Minister Zhao Qian, Grand Herald Huangfu Fu, Imperial Household Grandee Xue Zan, Fufeng Administrator Duan Keng, and several hundred civil and military fled to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred of Fu Jian's officials—among them Metropolitan Governor Quan Yi, Minister Zhao Qian, Grand Herald Huangfu Fu, Palace Grandee Xue Zan, and Fufeng prefect Duan Keng—rode to Yao Chang's camp.

sentences.zh: 萇遣驍騎將軍吳忠率騎圍堅，萇如新平。

translations.literal: Chang sent Fierce Cavalry General Wu Zhong to lead horse to surround Jian; Chang himself went to Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang sent Fierce Cavalry General Wu Zhong to ring Fu Jian with cavalry while he himself rode to Xinping.

sentences.zh: 俄而忠執堅，送之。

translations.literal: Soon Zhong seized Jian and delivered him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhong soon seized Fu Jian and brought him in.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖遣其車騎大將軍高蓋率眾五萬來伐，戰于新平南，大破之，蓋率麾下數千人來降，拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Murong Chong sent his Cavalry and Chariots Grand General Gao Gai to lead fifty thousand to attack; they fought south of Xinping, and he was greatly defeated; Gai led several thousand under his command to come surrender, and was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong ordered Gao Gai, his Cavalry and Chariots commander, against Yao Chang with fifty thousand men. South of Xinping Yao Chang shattered the army; Gao Gai brought a few thousand survivors over and was named Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 沖既率眾東下，長安空虛。

translations.literal: After Chong led his host eastward, Chang'an was empty.
translations.idiomatic: Once Murong Chong marched east, Chang'an stood hollowed out.

sentences.zh: 盧水郝奴稱帝于長安，渭北盡應之。

translations.literal: Lushui Hao Nu declared himself emperor in Chang'an, and all north of the Wei responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Nu of the Lushui tribes proclaimed himself emperor in Chang'an, and the north bank of the Wei rose at his call.

sentences.zh: 扶風王驎有眾數千，保據馬嵬。

translations.literal: Wang Lin of Fufeng had several thousand men and held Macang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin of Fufeng held Macang with a few thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 奴遣弟多攻驎。

translations.literal: Nu sent younger brother Duo to attack Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Nu sent his brother Duo against him.

sentences.zh: 萇伐驎，破之，驎走漢中。

translations.literal: Chang campaigned against Lin, defeated him, and Lin fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang struck Wang Lin, broke his line, and drove him into Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 執多而進攻奴，降之。

translations.literal: He seized Duo then advanced to attack Nu and made him surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Duo, then wheeled on Hao Nu and forced his submission.

sentences.zh: 乙太元十一年萇僭即皇帝位於長安，大赦，改元曰建初，國號大秦，改長安曰常安。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jin's Taiyuan era Chang usurpingly assumed the emperor's position at Chang'an, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era to Jianchu, took the state name Great Qin, and changed the name of the capital from Chang'an to Changan (常安, "Constant Peace").
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Taiyuan era Yao Chang seized the throne at Chang'an, ordered a general amnesty, adopted the reign name Jianchu, styled his state Great Qin, and renamed the capital Chang'an to Changan ("Constant Peace").

sentences.zh: 立妻虵氏為皇后，子興為皇太子，置百官。

translations.literal: He established wife She as empress, son Xing as heir apparent, and set up the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his consort of the She clan to empress, invested his son Yao Xing as crown prince, and filled out the imperial bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 自謂以火德承苻氏木行，服色如漢氏承周故事。

translations.literal: He claimed that by fire virtue he succeeded the Fu clan's wood phase, and dress colors followed Han's succeeding Zhou precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed the Mandate of Fire to follow Fu's Wood, and chose court colors by the Han precedent that had succeeded Zhou.

sentences.zh: 徙安定五千餘戶于長安。

translations.literal: He relocated more than five thousand households from An Ding to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He moved over five thousand Anding households into the capital.

sentences.zh: 以弟征虜緒為司隸校尉，鎮長安。

translations.literal: He made younger brother Conquering the Enemy Xu Metropolitan Governor and garrisoned Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his brother Yao Xu, General Who Conquers the Enemy, the metropolitan post and left him to hold Changan.

sentences.zh: 萇如安定，擊平涼胡金熙、鮮卑沒奕於，大破之。

translations.literal: Chang went to An Ding, attacked Pingliang Hu Jin Xi and Xianbei Moboyi Yu, and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang marched to Anding, smashed the Pingliang Di leader Jin Xi and the Xianbei chief Moboyi Yu, and scattered their hosts.

sentences.zh: 遂如秦州，與苻堅秦州刺史王統相持，天水屠各、略陽羌胡應萇者二萬餘戶，統懼，乃降。

translations.literal: Then he went to Qinzhou and stood off against Fu Jian's Qinzhou Inspector Wang Tong; Tuge of Tianshui and Qiang and Hu of Lüeyang who responded to Chang numbered more than twenty thousand households; Tong feared and then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed into Qinzhou against Fu Jian's inspector Wang Tong until Tianshui Tuge and Lüeyang Qiang and Hu—more than twenty thousand households—rallied to Yao Chang. Wang Tong, terrified, capitulated.

sentences.zh: 因饗將士於上邽，南安人古成詵進曰：「臣州人殷地險，俊傑如林，用武之國也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he feasted officers and soldiers at Shanggui; Gucheng Shen of Nan'an advanced and said: "My prefecture's people are abundant and the land rugged; outstanding men are like a forest—it is a state for wielding arms.
translations.idiomatic: At a victory banquet in Shanggui, Gucheng Shen of Nan'an spoke up: "My home commandery is populous, its terrain cruel, its heroes thick as trees—a land born for war."

sentences.zh: 王秦州不能收拔賢才，三分鼎足，而坐玩珠玉，以至於此。

translations.literal: Prince Qinzhou could not gather and elevate worthy talent or form a tripartite tripod stance, but sat fondling pearls and jade, until it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Inspector Wang never gathered men fit to divide the realm three ways; he sat fondling gems until ruin found him.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜散秦州金帛以施六軍，旌賢表善以副鄙州之望。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to distribute Qinzhou's gold and silk to supply the six armies, honor the worthy and display the good, to match my humble prefecture's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Scatter Qinzhou's gold and silk among the hosts, honor the able and the loyal, and you will answer what my people pray for.

sentences.zh: 」萇善之，擢為尚書郎。

translations.literal: " Chang approved and promoted him to Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang agreed and raised him to a secretariat post.

sentences.zh: 拜弟碩德都督隴右諸軍事、征西將軍、秦州刺史，領護東羌校尉，鎮上邽。

translations.literal: He appointed younger brother Shuo de Area Commander-in-Chief of Longyou, General Who Conquers the West, Qinzhou Inspector, concurrently Colonel Who Protects the Eastern Qiang, and garrisoned Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: He named his brother Yao Shuode commander of Longyou, General Who Conquers the West, Qinzhou inspector, and Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, with headquarters at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 萇還安定，修德政，布惠化，省非急之費，以救時弊，閭閻之士有豪介之善者，皆顯異之。

translations.literal: Chang returned to An Ding, cultivated virtuous government, spread beneficent transformation, cut non-urgent expenses to remedy the times' ills, and for gentlemen of the lanes who had heroic integrity's goodness he all distinguished them exceptionally.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Anding he pursued humane rule, spread relief, slashed needless spending, and singled out commoners of stubborn integrity for honor.

sentences.zh: 萇復如秦州，為苻登所敗，語在《登傳》。

translations.literal: Chang again went to Qinzhou, was defeated by Fu Deng—the account is in Deng's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang returned to Qinzhou and lost to Fu Deng, as told in Deng's memoir.

sentences.zh: 以其太子興鎮長安，而與登相距。

translations.literal: He posted his heir Xing to garrison Chang'an while he opposed Deng at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: He left crown prince Yao Xing to hold Changan while he faced Fu Deng in the field.

sentences.zh: 登馮翊太守蘭犢與苻師奴離貳，慕容永攻之，犢遣使請救。

translations.literal: Deng's Fengyi Administrator Lan Du and Fu Shinu were at odds; Murong Yong attacked him; Du sent envoys asking rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng's Fengyi prefect Lan Du had broken with Fu Shinu; Murong Yong fell upon Lan Du, who begged Yao Chang for aid.

sentences.zh: 萇將赴救，尚書令姚旻、左僕射尹緯等言於萇曰：「苻登近在瓦亭，陛下未宜輕舉。

translations.literal: Chang was about to go to the rescue; Director of the Secretariat Yao Min, Left Vice Director Yin Wei, and others said to Chang: "Fu Deng is near at Wating; Your Majesty ought not move lightly.
translations.idiomatic: As Yao Chang prepared to march, Yao Min and Yin Wei warned him, "Fu Deng sits close at Wating; this is no moment for a rash advance."

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「登遲重少決，每失時機，聞吾自行，正當廣集兵資，必不能輕軍深入。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Deng is sluggish and heavy, seldom decisive, always misses the moment for action; hearing I march myself, he will only broadly gather troops and supplies—he certainly cannot with a light army push deep.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang answered, "Fu Deng is slow and hesitant; he always misses his moment. If he hears I have taken the field he will hoard supplies and dare not strike deep with a light column."

sentences.zh: 兩月之間，足可克此三豎，吾事必矣。

translations.literal: Within two months it is enough to overcome these three wretches—my affair is settled.
translations.idiomatic: Two months will suffice to break those three upstarts; then the way is clear for me.

sentences.zh: 」遂師次於渥源。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the army halted at Woyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped the army at Woyuan.

sentences.zh: 師奴率眾來距，大戰，敗之，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Shinu led the host to oppose; they fought a great battle, defeated him, and took all his host captive.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shinu marched to meet him; Yao Chang shattered his line and took every survivor.

sentences.zh: 又擒蘭犢，收其士馬。

translations.literal: He also seized Lan Du and collected his soldiers and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Lan Du as well and absorbed his cavalry.

sentences.zh: 萇乃掘苻堅屍，鞭撻無數，裸剝衣裳，薦之以棘，坎土而埋之。

translations.literal: Chang then dug up Fu Jian's corpse, whipped it countless times, stripped the clothing naked, laid it on thorns, and buried it in earthen pit.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang had Fu Jian's corpse dug up, flogged it beyond counting, stripped it bare, rolled it on brambles, and heaped earth over the ruin.

sentences.zh: 慕容永征西將軍王宣率眾降萇。

translations.literal: Murong Yong's General Who Conquers the West Wang Xuan led the host to surrender to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuan, Murong Yong's western commander, brought his army over to Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 初，關西雄傑以苻氏既終，萇雄略命世，天下之事可一旦而定。

translations.literal: At first, heroes west of the Pass thought the Fu clan was already ended, Chang's heroic strategy commanded the age, and the realm's affairs could be settled in a morning.
translations.idiomatic: Once, every champion beyond the Pass believed Fu was finished and Yao Chang's genius owned the hour—that the empire could be settled in a single dawn.

sentences.zh: 萇既與苻登相持積年，數為登所敗，遠近咸懷去就之計，唯征虜齊難、冠軍徐洛生、輔國劉郭單、冠威彌姐婆觸、龍驤趙惡地、鎮北梁國兒等守忠不貳，並留子弟守營，供繼軍糧，身將精卒，隨萇征伐。

translations.literal: After Chang had faced Fu Deng for accumulated years, repeatedly was defeated by Deng, far and near all harbored plans of staying or leaving; only Conquering the Enemy Qi Nan, Champion Xu Luosheng, Support of the State Liu Guodan, Crown Might Mijie Potu, Dragon-Soaring Zhao Wudi, Garrison the North Liang Guo'er, and others kept loyalty undivided; together they left sons and younger brothers to guard camp, supplied successive army grain, personally led picked troops, and followed Chang on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Years of stalemate with Fu Deng, and repeated defeat, made allies far and near weigh betrayal—yet Qi Nan, Xu Luosheng, Liu Guodan, Mijie Potu, Zhao Wudi, Liang Guo'er, and a handful of others never wavered, left sons to guard their camps, fed Yao Chang's army, and rode with him in person.

sentences.zh: 時諸營既多，故號萇軍為大營，大營之號自此始也。

translations.literal: At the time the various camps were already many, therefore Chang's army was styled the Great Camp—the title Great Camp began from this.
translations.idiomatic: So many satellite camps sprang up that men called Yao Chang's host the Great Camp—a name born in those days.

sentences.zh: 時天大雪，萇下書深自責罰，散後宮文綺珍寶以供戎事，身食一味，妻不重彩。

translations.literal: At the time heaven snowed heavily; Chang issued a document deeply blaming and punishing himself, scattered rear-palace patterned silks and treasures to supply military affairs, himself ate one flavor, wives wore no heavy colors.
translations.idiomatic: When blizzards struck he published a self-rebuke, auctioned the harem's silks and jewels for the war chest, ate a single plain dish, and forbade his consorts rich dress.

sentences.zh: 將帥死王事者，加秩二等，士卒戰沒，皆有褒贈。

translations.literal: For generals who died in royal service, ranks were raised two grades; for soldiers fallen in battle, all had posthumous honors and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Generals who died in service gained two extra ranks of pension; every common soldier killed in action received a stipend for his kin.

sentences.zh: 立太學，禮先賢之後。

translations.literal: He established the Imperial Academy and honored the descendants of former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He founded an imperial academy and endowed the heirs of ancient sages.

sentences.zh: 敦煌索盧曜請刺苻登，萇曰：「卿以身徇難，將為誰乎？

translations.literal: Dunhuang Suolu Yao asked to assassinate Fu Deng; Chang said: "You use your body to die for hardship—for whom will it be?
translations.idiomatic: Suolu Yao of Dunhuang volunteered to murder Fu Deng. Yao Chang asked, "You mean to throw your life away—but for whose gain?"

sentences.zh: 」曜曰：「臣死之後，深以友人隴西辛暹仰托。

translations.literal: " Yao said: "After your servant dies, I deeply entrust to you my friend Longxi Xin Xian, looking up.
translations.idiomatic: Suolu Yao replied, "When I am gone, let my friend Xin Xian of Longxi take my place in your service."

sentences.zh: 」萇遣之。

translations.literal: " Chang sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang let him go.

sentences.zh: 事發，為登所殺，萇以暹為騎都尉。

translations.literal: When the affair broke, Deng killed him; Chang appointed Xian Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The plot surfaced; Fu Deng executed him, and Yao Chang named Xin Xian a cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 登進逼安定，諸將勸萇決戰，萇曰：「與窮寇競勝，兵家之下。

translations.literal: Deng advanced pressing An Ding; generals urged Chang to fight a decisive battle; Chang said: "With a cornered foe competing for victory is the lowest of the military art.
translations.idiomatic: As Fu Deng closed on Anding his generals demanded a pitched battle. Yao Chang refused. "To wrestle a desperate enemy for glory is the meanest stratagem in the canon."

sentences.zh: 吾將以計取之。

translations.literal: I will take him by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to break him by craft.

sentences.zh: 」於是留其尚書令姚旻守安定，夜襲登輜重於大界，克之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he left his Director of the Secretariat Yao Min to guard An Ding, night-raided Deng's baggage train at Dajie, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He left Yao Min to hold Anding, slipped by night against Fu Deng's baggage column at Dajie, and overran it.

sentences.zh: 諸將或欲因登駭亂擊之，萇曰：「登眾雖亂，怒氣猶盛，未可輕也。

translations.literal: Some generals wished to strike Deng while he was panic-stricken and in disorder; Chang said: "Though Deng's host is in disorder, angry qi is still strong—he cannot be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged a follow-up blow while Fu Deng reeled. Yao Chang said no: "His ranks may waver, but their rage still runs high—do not despise them."

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He held his hand.

sentences.zh: 萇以安定地狹，且逼苻登，使姚碩德鎮安定，徙安定千餘家安于陰密，遣弟征南靖鎮之。

translations.literal: Because An Ding's territory was narrow and Deng pressed close, Chang had Yao Shuo de garrison An Ding, relocated more than a thousand households from An Ding and settled them at Yinmi, and sent younger brother Conquering the South Jing to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Anding was cramped under Fu Deng's shadow, so Yao Chang stationed Yao Shuode there, moved a thousand Anding families into Yinmi, and sent his brother Yao Jing, General Who Conquers the South, to hold the new line.

sentences.zh: 立社稷于長安。

translations.literal: He established the altars of soil and grain at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He dedicated the state altars at Changan.

sentences.zh: 百姓年七十有德行者，拜為中大夫，歲賜牛酒。

translations.literal: For commoners aged seventy who had virtuous conduct, he appointed them Central Grand Masters and yearly gifted oxen and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners past seventy known for virtue were named grand counselors of the palace and given oxen and wine each year.

sentences.zh: 尹緯、姚晃謂古成詵曰：「苻登窮寇，歷年未滅，奸雄鴟峙，所在糾扇，夷夏皆貳，將若之何？

translations.literal: Yin Wei and Yao Huang said to Gucheng Shen: "Fu Deng is a cornered foe, years without being destroyed; traitors stand like hawks, everywhere gather and fan; barbarian and Chinese both are double-minded—what shall be done?
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei and Yao Huang asked Gucheng Shen, "Fu Deng still survives after all these years; every strongman preens like a hawk and fans revolt; tribesmen and Chinese alike waver—what now?"

sentences.zh: 」詵曰：「主上權略無方，信賞必罰，賢能之士，咸懷樂推，豈慮大業不成，氐賊不滅乎！

translations.literal: " Shen said: "Our lord's stratagem has no bound, trust rewards and sure punishments; men of worth and ability all harbor willing praise—why worry great enterprise will not succeed or Di rebels will not be destroyed!
translations.idiomatic: Gucheng Shen answered, "Our lord's designs know no limit; he rewards faith and punishes without mercy; every able man gladly lifts him up. Why doubt the great work—or that the Di bandit will fall?"

sentences.zh: 」緯曰：「登窮寇未滅，奸雄所在扇合，吾等寧無懼乎？

translations.literal: " Wei said: "Deng cornered foe not destroyed, traitors everywhere fan and unite—should we have no fear?
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei pressed him: "While Fu Deng lives and rogues flock everywhere, should we not be afraid?"

sentences.zh: 」詵曰：「三秦天府之國，主上十分已有其八。

translations.literal: " Shen said: "The three Qin are Heaven's treasury-land; our lord already has eight of ten parts.
translations.idiomatic: Gucheng Shen said, "The three Qin are heaven's own granary; our lord already holds eight parts in ten."

sentences.zh: 今所在可慮者，苻登、楊定、雷惡地耳，自餘瑣瑣，焉足論哉！

translations.literal: Those to worry about now are only Fu Deng, Yang Ding, and Lei Wudi; the rest petty—how worth discussing!
translations.idiomatic: Only Fu Deng, Yang Ding, and Lei Wudi still matter; the rest are gnats unworthy of talk.

sentences.zh: 然惡地地狹眾寡，不足為憂。

translations.literal: Yet Lei Wudi's territory is narrow and his host is few—not enough to be a worry.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Wudi holds thin ground and few spears—hardly worth a second thought.

sentences.zh: 苻登藉烏合犬羊，偷存假息，料其智勇，非至尊之匹。

translations.literal: Fu Deng, relying on a mob mixed as dogs and sheep, furtively preserves a false respite; gauge his wit and courage—they are no match for the most exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng clings to a rabble no better than sheep, stealing breath on borrowed time; set his mind and mettle against yours, and he cannot rival the throne.

sentences.zh: 霸王之起，必有驅除，然後克定大業。

translations.literal: When a hegemon-king rises, there must be driving-off and clearing-away; only afterward can the great enterprise be settled.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of every conqueror clears the field of rivals; only then can the great work stand complete.

sentences.zh: 昔漢、魏之興也，皆十有餘年，乃能一同於海內，五六年間未為久也。

translations.literal: In old days the rise of Han and of Wei each took more than ten years before they could unify within the seas; five or six years is not to be reckoned long.
translations.idiomatic: The Han and the Wei each needed more than a decade to knit the realm into one. A span of five or six years is scarcely long to wait.

sentences.zh: 主上神略內明，英武外發，可謂無敵於天下耳，取登有餘力。

translations.literal: The sovereign's divine designs shine inward; heroic martial prowess issues outward—he may be called without peer under Heaven. Taking Deng leaves strength to spare.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord reads the field in silence and strikes with open might; none under Heaven can stand before him. Fu Deng would fall and still leave force in reserve.

sentences.zh: 願布德行仁，招賢納士，厲兵秣馬，以候天機。

translations.literal: I pray you spread virtue and enact benevolence, summon worthies and accept knights, sharpen weapons and feed horses, and await Heaven's turning moment.
translations.idiomatic: Spread humanity, gather the able, hone the blades, rest the steeds, and watch for the hour fate tilts your way.

sentences.zh: 如其鴻業不成者，詵請腰斬以謝明公。

translations.literal: If thus the great swan enterprise does not succeed, Shen asks to be cut at the waist to apologize to the enlightened duke.
translations.idiomatic: If that high design fails, I, Shen, beg to be halved at the waist to answer to you.

sentences.zh: 」緯言之於萇，萇大悅，賜詵爵關內侯。

translations.literal: " Wei reported this to Chang; Chang was greatly pleased and bestowed on Shen the rank of marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Wei relayed it to Yao Chang, who was delighted and enfeoffed Shen as a marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 雷惡地率眾降萇，拜為鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: Lei Ede led his host to surrender to Chang and was appointed General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Ede brought his troops over to Yao Chang, who named him General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 魏褐飛自稱大將軍、沖天王，率氐胡數萬人攻安北姚當城於杏城，雷惡地應之，攻鎮東姚漢得于李潤。

translations.literal: Wei Hefei styled himself Grand General and Heaven-Rushing King; he led tens of thousands of Di and Hu to attack Defender of the North Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng. Lei Ede answered him and struck General Who Guards the East Yao Hande at Lirun.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Wei Hefei declared himself Grand General and King Who Charges Heaven, then drove tens of thousands of Di and Hu against Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng. Lei Ede joined the move and hit Yao Hande at Lirun.

sentences.zh: 萇議將討之，群臣咸曰：「陛下不憂六十里苻登，乃憂六百里褐飛？

translations.literal: Chang deliberated on campaigning against them. The assembled officials all said: "Your Majesty does not fret over Fu Deng sixty li away, yet frets over Hefei six hundred li away?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang weighed a punitive march. His ministers said: "You lose no sleep over Fu Deng on your doorstep, but lose it over Hefei far down the road?"

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「登非可卒殄，吾城亦非登所能卒圖。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Deng cannot be snuffed out in a stroke, nor can my stronghold be taken from him in a stroke."
translations.idiomatic: " Yao Chang replied: "Fu Deng will not vanish overnight, and my walls will not fall to him overnight either."

sentences.zh: 惡地多智，非常人也。

translations.literal: Ede abounds in schemes; he is no ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Ede is cunning—no common soldier of fortune.

sentences.zh: 南引褐飛，東結董成，甘言美說以成奸謀，若得杏城、李潤，惡地據之，控制遠近，相為羽翼，長安東北非復吾有。

translations.literal: Southward he draws Hefei; eastward he binds Dong Cheng; with honeyed words he finishes treasonous plots. If he holds Xingcheng and Lirun, Ede will sit on them, command near and far, and pair wing to wing—then the northeast of Chang'an is no longer ours.
translations.idiomatic: He pulls Hefei from the south, ropes in Dong Cheng from the east, and sweet-talks his way through treason. Seize Xingcheng and Lirun and Lei Ede commands the approaches; wings locked, the northeast of Chang'an slips from our grasp.

sentences.zh: 」於是潛軍赴之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he moved his army in secret and hurried to them.
translations.idiomatic: So he stole a march with hidden troops.

sentences.zh: 萇時眾不滿二千，褐飛、惡地眾至數萬，氐胡赴之者首尾不絕。

translations.literal: At that time Chang's men numbered fewer than two thousand; Hefei's and Ede's ran to tens of thousands, and Di and Hu who flocked to them came in an unbroken train.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang had fewer than two thousand men; Hefei and Lei Ede mustered tens of thousands, with Di and Hu pouring in without end.

sentences.zh: 萇每見一軍至，輒有喜色。

translations.literal: Whenever Chang saw another host arrive, he showed a joyful face.
translations.idiomatic: Each time fresh rebels appeared, Yao Chang looked glad.

sentences.zh: 群下怪而問之，萇曰：「今同惡相濟，皆來會集，吾得乘勝席捲，一舉而覆其巢穴，東北無復餘也。

translations.literal: His subordinates marveled and asked him. Chang said: "Now evildoers aid one another and gather in one place; I may ride victory and roll them up like a mat, overturn their nest in one stroke, and leave nothing left in the northeast."
translations.idiomatic: His officers wondered aloud. Yao Chang said: "They flock together—traitors feeding traitors. I can sweep them in one rush, tear out the nest, and clear the whole northeast."

sentences.zh: 」褐飛等以萇兵少，盡眾來攻。

translations.literal: " Hefei and the others, because Chang's troops were few, brought their entire force to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking Yao Chang weak, Hefei threw every man forward.

sentences.zh: 萇固壘不戰，示之以弱，潛遣子崇率騎數百，出其不意，以乘其後。

translations.literal: Chang held fast behind his ramparts and would not fight, showing weakness; secretly he sent his son Chong with several hundred horse to slip out unlooked-for and strike their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang hugged his walls and feigned frailty, while his son Chong looped behind with a few hundred riders and hit them where they did not look.

sentences.zh: 褐飛兵擾亂，萇遣鎮遠王超、平遠譚亮率步騎擊之，褐飛眾大潰，斬褐飛及首級萬餘。

translations.literal: Hefei's troops were thrown into confusion. Chang sent Distant Pacifier Wang Chao and Far-Smoother Tan Liang with foot and horse to strike them; Hefei's host broke utterly. Hefei was beheaded, and more than ten thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Hefei's lines crumbled. Yao Chang sent Wang Chao and Tan Liang with mixed arms; the rebel army shattered. Hefei lost his head, and the tally passed ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 惡地請降，萇待之如初。

translations.literal: Ede asked to surrender; Chang treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Ede sued for peace, and Yao Chang welcomed him as if nothing had changed.

sentences.zh: 惡地每謂人曰：「吾自言智勇所施，足為一時之傑。

translations.literal: Ede often told people: "I have always said that where I apply wit and courage, I am enough to be a champion of the age."
translations.idiomatic: Lei Ede used to say: "Where I bring mind and nerve, I am fit to stand among the heroes of the hour."

sentences.zh: 校數諸雄，如吾之徒，皆應跨據一方，獸嘯千里。

translations.literal: Measured against the warlords, men like me ought to stride across one region and roar like beasts for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Stack me against the lords of the age: my kind should hold a quarter of the map and make the wilds echo for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 遇姚公智力摧屈，是吾分也。

translations.literal: Meeting Lord Yao, wit and strength were broken and bent—that is my portion.
translations.idiomatic: Then I met Lord Yao, and mind and might alike were broken—that was simply my lot.

sentences.zh: 」惡地猛毅清肅，不可幹以非義，嶺北諸豪皆敬憚之。

translations.literal: " Ede was fierce, resolute, clear, and stern; he could not be moved by what was unjust. The chiefs north of the ridges all honored and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Ede was grim, upright, and austere—no appeal to wrong could sway him. North of the passes every strongman respected and dreaded him.

sentences.zh: 萇命其將當城于營處一柵孔中蒔樹一根，以旌戰功。

translations.literal: Chang ordered his general Dangcheng to plant one tree in a gap of the palisade at the camp site, to mark the battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang told General Yao Dangcheng to set a single sapling in a hole in the stockade where they had camped, a living marker of the fight.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，問之，城曰：「營所至小，已廣之矣。

translations.literal: After more than a year he asked about it. Dangcheng said: "The camp ground was extremely small; I have already enlarged it."
translations.idiomatic: A year later he inquired. Dangcheng said: "The plot was tiny—I have widened it."

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「少來鬥戰無如此快，以千六百人破三萬眾，國之事業，由此克舉。

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Since youth I have never known fighting so brisk. With sixteen hundred men we broke a host of thirty thousand; the state's enterprise, by this, could be raised."
translations.idiomatic: " Yao Chang said: "I have never had a quicker fight. Sixteen hundred broke thirty thousand; the kingdom's fate turned on that stroke."

sentences.zh: 小乃為奇，大何足貴！」

translations.literal: Small, then, is marvelous; what greatness is worth prizing!"
translations.idiomatic: Small made the wonder—size would have cheapened it!"

sentences.zh: 貳城胡曹寅、王達獻馬三千匹。

translations.literal: The Hu of Ercheng, Cao Yin and Wang Da, presented three thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yin and Wang Da, Hu leaders of Ercheng, brought three thousand horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 以寅為鎮北將軍、并州刺史，達鎮遠將軍、金城太守。

translations.literal: Yin was made General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Bingzhou; Da was made General Who Distantly Pacifies and Administrator of Jincheng.
